name: Learn: Modify Existing Assets (tricky bits)
objective: CKAD exam-reality: questions hand you assets that ALREADY exist and ask you to change them. Goal: handle the non-obvious immutability quirks — relabel a Deployment (immutable selector), change a bare Pod (immutable in place), edit an on-disk manifest and re-apply, and make running pods pick up a changed ConfigMap.
description: Four pre-seeded assets in 'modify-learn', each needing a change that isn't a straight edit: an immutable Deployment selector, an immutable Pod, an on-disk YAML you must edit + apply, and a ConfigMap whose change only lands after a rollout restart.

questions.title: Relabel a Deployment (selector is immutable)
questions.teach:
A Deployment's `.spec.selector` is **immutable** — the API rejects any change to it after creation. So you cannot simply `kubectl edit` a Deployment to give it new labels: editing `selector.matchLabels` fails with `field is immutable`, and changing only the pod-template labels (so they no longer match the selector) is also rejected.

**To truly relabel, you recreate:**
- `kubectl delete deployment <name>` then re-create it with the new `selector` + matching template labels.
- Keep the pods alive during the swap with `kubectl delete deployment <name> --cascade=orphan` (orphans the ReplicaSet/pods), then recreate — advanced, rarely needed in the exam.
- `kubectl get deploy <name> -o yaml > d.yaml`, edit selector+labels, `kubectl replace --force -f d.yaml` (delete+recreate in one command).

**Gotchas:**
- `selector` is immutable; the pod-template labels must always be a **superset** of (i.e. match) the selector.
- A Service selects pods by label too — relabeling pods can silently detach them from a Service; update the Service selector to match.
- `kubectl label` changes labels on live objects but **cannot** change a Deployment's selector.
questions.prompt:
The Deployment `legacy` in `modify-learn` has selector and pod labels `app=legacy`. Relabel it so both its selector and its pods use `app=payments` instead.

Target: Deployment `legacy` exists with `.spec.selector.matchLabels.app=payments`, matching pod-template labels, and at least one available replica.
questions.hint: You can't edit the selector in place (it's immutable). Recreate: `kubectl -n modify-learn get deploy legacy -o yaml > /tmp/legacy.yaml`, change every `app: legacy` to `app: payments`, then `kubectl -n modify-learn replace --force -f /tmp/legacy.yaml`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n modify-learn get deploy legacy -o yaml > /tmp/legacy.yaml
sed -i '' 's/app: legacy/app: payments/g' /tmp/legacy.yaml   # (Linux: sed -i 's/.../g')
kubectl -n modify-learn replace --force -f /tmp/legacy.yaml
kubectl -n modify-learn get deploy legacy -o wide

verification.description: legacy recreated with selector+pods relabeled app=payments

questions.title: Change a bare Pod (immutable in place)
questions.teach:
A running **Pod** is almost entirely immutable. You can change only a few fields live — the container `image` (`kubectl set image pod/<name> …`), `spec.activeDeadlineSeconds`, `tolerations` (additions), and `spec.containers[*].resources` for in-place resize on newer clusters. **Everything else — env, command, volumes, labels-that-matter, most of the spec — cannot be edited**; `kubectl edit`/`kubectl apply` reject the change with `may not be changed`.

**To change an immutable field, recreate the Pod:**
- `kubectl get pod <name> -o yaml > p.yaml`, edit, then `kubectl replace --force -f p.yaml` (deletes + recreates in one step).
- Or `kubectl delete pod <name>` and re-create from an edited manifest.
- `kubectl run … --env=KEY=val --dry-run=client -o yaml` is a fast way to scaffold the new pod YAML.

**Gotchas:**
- `kubectl set env pod/<name> …` fails — `set env` works on templates (Deployments), not live Pods.
- This is exactly why you deploy via a **Deployment**: it recreates pods for you on a template change. A bare Pod has no controller to do that.
- `replace --force` is delete+recreate — the pod gets a new UID/IP and restarts from scratch.
questions.prompt:
A bare Pod `tool` (busybox) runs in `modify-learn`. Add an environment variable `MODE=prod` to its container.

Target: Pod `tool` is Running and its container has env `MODE=prod`.
questions.hint: You can't add env to a live Pod (`set env pod/...` and `edit` are rejected). Recreate it: `kubectl -n modify-learn get pod tool -o yaml > /tmp/tool.yaml`, add the env under the container, then `kubectl -n modify-learn replace --force -f /tmp/tool.yaml`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n modify-learn get pod tool -o yaml > /tmp/tool.yaml
# add under containers[0]:  env: [{name: MODE, value: prod}]
kubectl -n modify-learn replace --force -f /tmp/tool.yaml
kubectl -n modify-learn get pod tool -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].env}'

verification.description: pod tool recreated with env MODE=prod

questions.title: Edit an on-disk manifest and re-apply
questions.teach:
Exam assets often live as a **YAML file on disk** that's already applied to the cluster. You change the file, then re-apply — the file stays the source of truth.

**Edit → apply workflow:**
- `kubectl apply -f file.yaml` — declarative; records a `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation and does a three-way merge, so re-applying an edited file updates only what changed.
- `kubectl diff -f file.yaml` — preview exactly what will change **before** applying (huge in the exam).
- `kubectl edit` edits the *live* object but **not** your file — the two drift apart; prefer editing the file when a file is the asset.

**Gotchas:**
- `apply` on an object first created with `create`/`run` (imperative) warns about the missing last-applied annotation the first time — harmless, it adopts it.
- Fields you remove from the file are removed from the object on apply (three-way merge) — `edit`/`patch` don't do that.
- Keep `namespace` in the manifest or pass `-n`, or apply lands in the wrong namespace.
questions.prompt:
The manifest `/tmp/kindlab-assets/widget-deploy.yaml` defines Deployment `widget` (applied at 1 replica, `nginx:1.25`). Edit the **file** to scale it to `3` replicas and update the image to `nginx:1.26`, then apply it.

Target: Deployment `widget` in `modify-learn` has 3 available replicas on image `nginx:1.26`.
questions.hint: Edit `/tmp/kindlab-assets/widget-deploy.yaml` (set `replicas: 3` and `image: nginx:1.26`), preview with `kubectl diff -f /tmp/kindlab-assets/widget-deploy.yaml`, then `kubectl apply -f /tmp/kindlab-assets/widget-deploy.yaml`.
questions.solution:
sed -i '' -e 's/replicas: 1/replicas: 3/' -e 's/nginx:1.25/nginx:1.26/' /tmp/kindlab-assets/widget-deploy.yaml
kubectl diff -f /tmp/kindlab-assets/widget-deploy.yaml
kubectl apply -f /tmp/kindlab-assets/widget-deploy.yaml
kubectl -n modify-learn rollout status deployment/widget

verification.description: widget updated to 3 replicas + nginx:1.26 via the on-disk file

questions.title: Make pods pick up a changed ConfigMap
questions.teach:
A Deployment's pods read a ConfigMap value through `env … valueFrom.configMapKeyRef`. That env is resolved **once, at pod start** — so editing the ConfigMap does **not** change the value inside already-running pods. You must roll the pods.

**Apply a config change to running pods:**
- Update the ConfigMap: `kubectl create configmap <cm> --from-literal=K=v --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -` (or `kubectl edit configmap <cm>`).
- Then `kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name>` — new pods start and re-read the ConfigMap.

**Gotchas:**
- `env`/`envFrom` from a ConfigMap/Secret are **frozen at pod start**; only ConfigMaps mounted as a **volume** update live in the container (and even then the app must re-read the file).
- `rollout restart` is the clean way to reload config with no spec change; deleting pods one by one also works but is crude.
- An **immutable** ConfigMap (`immutable: true`) can't be edited at all — you must create a new one and point the Deployment at it.
- `kubectl set env deploy/<name> --from=configmap/<cm>` wires env to the CM but still needs a restart when the CM later changes.
questions.prompt:
Deployment `web` in `modify-learn` reads env `COLOR` from ConfigMap `web-config` (currently `blue`). Change the config to `green` and make the **running** pods actually serve `COLOR=green`.

Target: ConfigMap `web-config` has `COLOR=green` AND a running `web` pod reports `COLOR=green` from its environment.
questions.hint: Update the CM then roll the pods: `kubectl -n modify-learn create configmap web-config --from-literal=COLOR=green --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`, then `kubectl -n modify-learn rollout restart deployment/web`. Verify with `kubectl -n modify-learn exec <web-pod> -- printenv COLOR`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n modify-learn create configmap web-config --from-literal=COLOR=green --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n modify-learn rollout restart deployment/web
kubectl -n modify-learn rollout status deployment/web
kubectl -n modify-learn exec deploy/web -- printenv COLOR   # green

verification.description: web-config=green AND running web pods serve COLOR=green (needed a restart)
